Brenda, John — thank you for having us through. The short version first.

We bring a bin and a crew and empty the house. You lift nothing, and it costs you nothing. Then we clean it, inspect it, photograph it, and put it in front of buyers — five to seven days from the bin arriving to live on the market, and about two weeks from there to offers in hand. Everything that follows is the evidence behind the number, and the number is lower than you are hoping. We would rather tell you that now.

What we do for you

Step one: we empty the house. You lift nothing and you pay nothing for it.

THE BIN ARRIVES FIRST. Before a single photograph is taken we put a bin on your driveway and bring a crew in to clear everything you are not keeping. That is a $3,000 to $4,000 job and we cover it.

From the bin arriving to the house being live on the market is five to seven days. From there to offers in hand is about two weeks.

STEP 1 — We empty the house

SYNERGY's own MLS® extract, January 1 – September 30, 2026: 45,564 sales across 26 municipalities, freehold and condominium. The vertical axis starts at $800,000 rather than zero so the movement is readable.

This is the whole market, not one neighbourhood — 45,564 sales across 26 municipalities this year.

It peaked in the spring and has come down since. Volume is off a quarter from June. Price per square foot, which is the fairest measure because it takes the size of the house out of the comparison, is down 4.1% from April; freehold is down 4.3% and condominiums 5.7%. Average and median sale prices are both down about six per cent from May.

Borrowing has tightened at the same time. The Bank of Canada has held its rate at 2.25%, but a buyer's budget is set by the fixed rate, which is priced off the bond market rather than the Bank. Five-year yields rose through early October and lenders followed — BMO went up 20 points to 5.14% on October 7.

Pickering detached has held up better than the market as a whole, but it is one segment of it and it is not insulated from it. The direction of travel is the reason not to spend four months on renovations before selling.

Section 04 · What these sales tell us

658 Cognac is your house. The rest show what condition and setting are worth.

658 Cognac Crescent — the same floorplan as yours

$1,025,000

2,473 sq ft · identical builder layout · renovated and staged · sold March 2026

Two copies of the same house, and the photographs tell you the rest. Theirs was renovated and professionally staged — white kitchen with stone counters, updated bathrooms, hardwood throughout — with a partly finished basement carrying a two-piece bath and a rough-in for a shower. Yours is original through most of the house with an unfinished basement and no rough-in. They sit on an interior street on a lot less than half the size of yours; you face the road on a corner with a hydro corridor behind. $1,025,000 is what this floorplan fetches finished. Two routes, deliberately. One works down from a renovated copy of your own house; the other works up from the only sale this year that shared your condition and your unfinished basement. They approach from opposite directions and do not quite meet — the gap between them is about $50,000, and that gap is the honest measure of how much uncertainty sits in a house like this.

We weight the second more heavily. Adjusting down from a renovated home means estimating what a full renovation is worth, which is the least reliable number anyone can put in a document like this. Adjusting up from 1911 Rosebank means two small, concrete adjustments — size and setting — from a house that was genuinely in your condition.

Built from records, the listing photographs and one visit — no rooms measured and no mechanicals inspected. An inspection could move this either way, which is why we pay for one before the house goes up rather than letting a buyer's inspector set the agenda.

What we list it at is a separate decision, and a strategic one. It is not the same number as the value, and it is the conversation to have in person. It is the first item under next steps.

Section 07 · Who buys a home like yours

Two buyers, and both want exactly what you have.

The gap between a house that needs work and a fully renovated one at this size stands at $150,000 and up — and that is only the money. On top of it sit the carrying costs while the work is done, the months it takes, the stress of running it, and the risk that it costs more than planned or lands in a worse market.

Whoever buys this house takes all five of those on. That is what the price reflects, and it is exactly what you avoid by selling it as it stands.

The contractor or investor

They price the work rather than fear it. A 100 amp panel and a 2007 furnace are line items, and the roof already being done is what makes the file work. The side entrance from the garage, with room for a walk-up, is the detail that decides it. With nine listings your size on the market and not one of them a project, they have nowhere else to go.

The family renovating to stay

Trading up within Amberlea, often with parents to accommodate. They want the schools, a lot they can do something with, and a layout they can change. The land matters to this buyer in a way it does not to the market generally — across 168 sales, lot size barely moves the price at all.

Who will not buy it

The buyer who wants to move in and change nothing. They are served by the homes asking $1,095,000 and up. Chasing them is how a house ends up where 552 Steeple Hill ended up.

What happens next

A pricing strategy session first.

Nothing here commits you to anything. The valuation is in Section 05; what we list it at is a different decision, and a strategic one. That is the conversation to have together.

Step one · the pricing strategy sessionHalf an hour at your kitchen table. We go through this document, then the part that is not in it — what to list at, whether to set a date for reviewing offers, and how we bring several buyers through on the same weekend rather than waiting for one. There is more than one way to do this and the right answer depends on what matters most to you.
Step two · you decide what you are keepingWalk the house and set aside what comes with you. Everything else is ours to handle.
Step three · we empty itBin on the driveway, crew in, professional clean. At our cost.
Step four · we prepare itPre-listing inspection, photography, video and drone, floor plans. Five to seven days from the bin arriving.
Step five · we launch itLive on MLS®, open houses both weekend days, and offers reviewed on the date we agreed. You will hear from us throughout, not only when there is news.

From the day you say go, roughly two weeks to offers in hand.
